reader.requirement: At --std 85, FUNCTION INTEGER's argument-1 must be class numeric, i.e. an arithmetic expression (A.2.2 type 1: identifiers of numeric elementary items, numeric literals, expressions); an alphanumeric, alphabetic, numeric-edited (class alphanumeric in 1985), group, nonnumeric-literal or nonnumeric figurative argument must be refused, and every numeric form must be accepted and floored.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 edition window: IntrinsicSig.IntroducedIn (85 for the 1989 module rows) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel, COBOL1502/COBOL1503
ArgPredicate.AppliesAt(edition year) gates the per-position predicates (CharacterCategory etc.); the class-kind test itself is edition-invariant

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|Version|AppliesAt in IntrinsicBinder.cs and IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs; INTEGER's Verified row is Uniform('n') with no predicates, so no edition-gated predicate applies
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1_integer_floor_85 exercises only accepted DISPLAY S9V99 items; the refusal half (alphanumeric item/literal, numeric-edited, group, alphabetic, SPACE, ALL literal), COMP/COMP-3, subscripted, expression, ZERO and 18-digit operands are not exercised

probes.printed: COBOL1627 on each of INTEGER(X alnum), INTEGER("12"), INTEGER(NE numeric-edited), INTEGER(G group), INTEGER(AL alphabetic), INTEGER(SPACE), INTEGER(ALL "1") (plus an unrelated COBOL0900 for my VALUE 1.5 on a numeric-edited item, correct at 85)
probes.expected: each argument is not class numeric -> refused (A.2.15.3 AR1)

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.15.3 AR1  (2.15.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR1
OK  §1989:A.2.2  (2.2 ARGUMENTS**)  the text is in the clause; it lies in AR1 ('An arithmetic expression must be specified')
OK  §1989:A.2.15.4 RV1  (2.15.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV1

reader.notes: The class screen is the catalog-driven CheckArgumentClasses over the spec-verified Verified table (INTEGER = Uniform('n')); it runs identically at every edition. Every non-numeric operand class is refused with COBOL1627 at --std 85 and every numeric form is accepted and floored correctly. The diagnostic text cites §2023 clauses, which is cosmetic.

refuter.evidence: rint1.cob (--compile-only, --std 85): INTEGER(index data item IX) COBOL6979 citing §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR5; INTEGER(index-name XN) COBOL1637; INTEGER(N(1:2)) on a PIC 9(4) item COBOL1627 class alphanumeric (right: ref-modification of a numeric item is class alphanumeric at 1985); INTEGER(88 C1) COBOL1639; INTEGER(FUNCTION CHAR(50)) COBOL1627; INTEGER(HIGH-VALUE) and INTEGER(QUOTE) COBOL1627. rint2.cob runs: SQRT(2)->1, INTEGER-PART(-12.345)->-12, -12.345->-13, SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -7->-7, COMP S9(18) -999999999999999999 unchanged, S9PPP -5000->-5000, SPP9 -0.005->-1, ZEROES->0, unary -N->12, N**2=152.399->152, each right per RV1. cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.15.3 AR1 'Argument-1 must be class numeric'; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5 (ref-mod of numeric is class alphanumeric); OK §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR5; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR1.
